items.title: Dipole moment and polarity of molecules

source_refs.note: The unnumbered topic Dipole Moment and Polarity of Molecules, printed pages 51-52 (Figures 3.5 to 3.7), with Quick Check 3.4 as the self-check.

blocks.text: In compounds such as HF, where the bonded atoms are from different elements, the electronic distribution between the atoms is uneven. Due to this reason, one atom carries partial positive and the other negative charge.

blocks.title: Dipole
blocks.text: A molecule with δ⁺ charge on one part and δ⁻ charge on the other part is called a dipole and such a molecule is said to have a dipole moment.

It is a quantitative measurement of the polarity of a bond or a molecule. The dipole moments of diatomic molecules like HF, HCl, HBr, HI, NO, etc. are directed from the positive ends (δ⁺) to negative ends (δ⁻) as in Fig. 3.5. Dipole moment is measured in Debye unit (D). Higher dipole moment indicates high polarity in a molecule.

blocks.alt: Left: a dot picture of the electron cloud of HF, thicker around the fluorine nucleus than the hydrogen nucleus. Right: H (delta+) bonded to a larger F (delta-), with a crossed arrow drawn from the H end to the F end showing the dipole.
blocks.caption: Electron density in HF is higher near F; the dipole moment points from H to F (original diagram after Figure 3.5).

blocks.text: For compounds having more than two atoms, the dipole moment depends on the structure of the molecule. The dipole moment of water is 1.85 D which is directed from the end having two hydrogen atoms to the end with the oxygen atom as in the structure shown in Fig. 3.6. A linear H₂O molecule (H-O-H) would have zero dipole moment. The non-zero dipole moment value shows that water is a non-linear molecule. Experiments reveal that the water molecule has a v-shaped structure. In contrast, SO₂ has a dipole moment of 1.61 D and in opposite direction to that in water. H₂S is also a non-linear molecule as the individual bonds are polar, but they don’t cancel each other’s dipole moment and the overall molecule has some dipole moment.

blocks.alt: Left: a bent H2O molecule with delta- on O and delta+ on each H; bond-moment arrows point from H to O and the resultant points up to O; P = 1.85 D. Right: a bent SO2 molecule with delta+ on S and delta- on each O; the bond-moment arrows point from S to O and the resultant points down, away from S; P = 1.61 D. Below: a coloured electron density map of water, red at the oxygen end and blue at the hydrogen end, with the printed note that the dipole moment is from blue to red.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.6: Vector addition of individual bond moments in angular H2O and SO2 molecules (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.6).

blocks.text: However, some molecules have zero dipole moments as the symmetry in their structures causes the cancellation of the individual bond moments. For example, BeCl₂ is a linear molecule having two similar Cl atoms on both sides of the central atom at 180°. The individual Be-Cl bond moments are cancelled out as they are opposite in direction and equal in amount. Similarly, CCl₄ has four C-Cl bonds which are expected to have high polarity due to a large electronegativity difference between C and Cl atoms. The bond moments associated to the four C-Cl bonds are directed in such a way that they cancel each other. The net dipole moment of the CCl₄ molecule is zero making it a non-polar molecule. The CCl₄ molecule is perfectly tetrahedral. Similarly, BF₃ has a trigonal planar symmetrical structure and its dipole moment is also zero. As a rule, the molecules that have same ligands (atoms or groups of atoms with the central atom) in a regular geometry, the individual dipole moments may not be zero, but overall molecule has zero dipole moment. Such a molecule is said to be non-polar.

blocks.alt: Three symmetrical molecules, each with p = 0 D beneath it. BeCl2 is linear, Cl-Be-Cl, with a 180 degree arc. BF3 is trigonal with delta+ on B, delta- on each F and a bond-moment arrow beside each B-F bond pointing to F. CCl4 is drawn as a tetrahedral sketch with delta+ on C, delta- on each Cl and a bond-moment arrow beside each C-Cl bond pointing to Cl. The moments cancel.
blocks.caption: Figure 3.7: The individual bond moments in symmetrical molecules BeCl2, BF3 and CCl4 cancel out to give zero net dipole moment (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 3.7; the printed caption says CH4).

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The printed caption names CH₄, while the figure and the text show CCl₄; the caption above names CCl₄.
